evidence.text: In plain words: when you approve a client's CV, the approval is meant to lock in exactly the files that made that PDF, so the CV you send is the CV you checked. Until tonight a custom CV that kept extra facts in a side file either failed to build from its saved copy or quietly read the live file, which could change after you approved; now every file the CV reads is saved with the revision, and a CV that still reads a live file cannot be approved.

evidence.command: python tests/run.py (on main after all merges), workflow step 10
evidence.excerpt:
PASS: 52 compilation cases plus PDF/data/layout assertions.
One-off tour-guide CV (Framework only, 1 page): presentation.json, parts/helper.typ, parts/note.txt, parts/link.txt copied and hashed; compiles again after the live files are deleted.
REFUSED: cv.typ reads /private/zz-fictional/presentation.json by a root-absolute path, so a revision would read the live file, not a snapshot; write the path relative to cv.typ
REFUSED: cv.typ reads ../outside.json, which is outside the workspace; ...
REFUSED: cv.typ reads assets/portrait.png, which is not the portrait but would take its place in the snapshot; rename one of them
Computed live read: checks fail -> REFUSED: Revision ...: automated checks failed (The compile read ...presentation.json, a live file outside the revision snapshot ...)

feedback.title: Multi-select questions
feedback.body: A question about which of several items to keep is naturally multi-select (keep A and B, drop C). The ask command documents only single-choice options with one recommended id, so the agent had to recommend one item and let the developer add the second in a note. A 'multiple: true' flag with a recommended list would fit such keep/drop questions.
